patch.summary: WebCatalog migration guide: inventory → rehearse → freeze → validate integrations — grounded in researched limitations and catalogue peers.

blocks.body: Migrate to WebCatalog by inventorying legacy project-management fields, mapping them to WebCatalog objects, rehearsing a freeze window, and validating Chrome, Macos, Windows before reopening writes.
bullets: Inventory → map → rehearse → cut over → reopen
Highest risk: Adjacent desktop shell — not a project management or work OS tool
Success signal: primary workflow works for the pilot cohort

blocks.heading: WebCatalog migration cutover playbook
blocks.body: Migrations fail from optimistic timelines — not from missing motivation.

scenarios.title: Field inventory
scenarios.body: Export legacy fields that power revenue workflows and mark must-map vs archive.

scenarios.title: Rehearsal load
scenarios.body: Run a non-prod load into WebCatalog; measure match rates before the freeze.

scenarios.title: Production freeze
scenarios.body: Freeze legacy writes; cut over; validate Chrome; then reopen.

steps.label: Migrate when Knowledge workers who want web apps as desktop apps / workspaces outweigh migration cost
Delay if this limitation hits cutover: Adjacent desktop shell — not a project management or work OS tool
If WebCatalog mapping is poor, compare destination fit with monday.com before moving data twice

items.title: No freeze window
items.body: Dual-writing without a freeze creates irrevocable duplicates.

items.title: Integrations last
items.body: Wire Chrome in rehearsal — not on Monday morning after cutover.

items.title: Data risk 1
items.body: Adjacent desktop shell — not a project management or work OS tool

items.title: Data risk 3
items.body: No boards, Gantt, automations, or PM reporting

checklist.label: Complete field inventory for core workflows
Mitigate: Adjacent desktop shell — not a project management or work OS tool
